summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies, John Snelling served as General Secretary of the Buddhist Society from around 1980 to 1984 and edited The Middle Way from around 1980 to 1990.

John Stevenson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Glasgow and the University of Edinburgh. He served with the Scottish Missionary Society and East India Company, founded the Bombay Gazette, and led the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

John Stirling Morley Hooper studied at the University of Oxford and Corpus Christi College. Working in Indology and religious studies, he was Headmaster of Wesley Higher Secondary School in 1930 and General Secretary of the Bible Society of India in 1941.

Linguist John Strachan studied at Aberdeen, Cambridge, and Jena under Berthold Delbrück and Rudolf Thurneysen. A fellow at Pembroke College, Cambridge, he served as Professor of Greek (1885) and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology (1889) at Owens College.

John Stratton Hawley, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied at Amherst College and completed his doctorate under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He taught at Bowdoin College before becoming Claire Tow Professor of Religion at Columbia University around 1986.
John Stuart Mill worked in philosophy, history, and archaeology. He studied at University College London from around 1828 to 1830 and served with the East India Company from around 1823 to 1858.

John Sydenham Furnivall, a scholar in history and archaeology, studied at Cambridge, Trinity Hall, Trinity College, and Leiden University. He founded the Burma Research Society in 1910 and held a post at the University of Cambridge from around 1936 to 1941.

John Taber, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl. He taught at Case Western Reserve University from around 1983 to 1989 and joined the University of New Mexico.
John Taylor worked in Indology and philosophy. He earned an M.D. from the University of Edinburgh by 1804 and held a post with the London Missionary Society from 1805 to 1807.

An Indologist, John Thayer Hitchcock studied at Amherst, Chicago, Connecticut, and Cornell. After teaching at Amherst, UC Berkeley, and UCLA, he was Professor of Anthropology and South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1966 to 1982.

John Thompson Platts, an expert in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, was educated at Bedford School and Balliol College. He held posts at Benares College and Saugor High School before teaching Persian at Oxford in 1880.

John Van Someren Pope, a scholar in Indology and linguistics, earned an M.A. at the University of Cambridge. He served as Professor at Presidency University from around 1876 to 1884 and Reader in Modern East Indian Languages at Trinity College Dublin.
John Victor Boulton, a scholar in Indology and linguistics, earned his Ph.D. at SOAS University of London around 1961–1967 and served there as Lecturer in Bengali and Oriya from 1962 to 1988.

John Vincent Bellezza is a researcher in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel, and held a post attested in 2014 at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, John W. Pettit completed his undergraduate studies at Haverford College. He studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa, and doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman.

John W. Schroeder, working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earned his Ph.D. at the University of Oregon under Don Levi. He taught at Oregon and the College of Wooster, joining St. Mary's College of Maryland as an assistant professor in 1996.

John W. Spellman was an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham from around 1958 to 1960. He held posts at the University of Washington (around 1964–1967) and the University of Windsor (around 1967–1999).

Indologist and historian John Watson McCrindle was educated at the University of Edinburgh. He served as Principal of Doveton College, Professor at Krishnagar Government College, Fellow at the University of Calcutta, and Principal of Patna College from 1867 to 1880.
John Wenger was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Bern in 1827 and obtained a D.D. from the University of Rhode Island around 1878.

John Whalen-Bridge, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, studied at Connecticut, UC Davis, and USC. He taught at the University of the Ryukyus (1993–1998) and became an Associate Professor at the National University of Singapore in 1998.
